doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: Learning harmonica and playing in the subway
summary: Mending a broken heart, she picked up a musician's harmonica and played between subway cars, then busked with an old man from Mississippi.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: was mending my heart over a heartbreak and it was a musician who one of his instruments was the harmonica. So it was sitting on this table and one day we were listening to “Sugar Blue” and I picked it up and I started just – and he goes, you know, “Baby you got something.” And it was like I got bit by that. I would get on the trains, the express train from 96th Street to 14th Street – well my kids – I was a single parent – while my kids were in school. And I would play between the cars so I wouldn’t disturb anyone. I’d have Muddy Waters on, you know in my headphones, and I would just wail, like outside in the tunnel that connects the cars. So I’d be bouncing up and down holding on with one hand and just practicing my heart out. And then I met the old man, and that was it. I couldn’t have been happier and I started making enough money. I produced a little CD for us from our live recordings, and I started making enough money to support it. I was making like 800 a week off the books. Yes. You know, not too many little sidemen in New York can do that in the train station. Back in time for dinner. Didn’t even need a babysitter.
